claims.text: In-situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction integrated with a high-temperature environmental chamber allows real-time tracking of oxidation kinetics.
The integrated method allows real-time tracking of phase transformations under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
The integrated method captures transient intermediates that ex-situ methods miss.
High-temperature oxidizing conditions induce oxidation reactions.
Oxidation under the specified high-temperature conditions is accompanied by phase transitions.
Transient and evolving crystalline phases can be tracked through XRD peak shifts and intensities.
In-situ synchrotron XRD captures rapid, transient changes in crystal structure in real time.
Real-time XRD patterns will reveal transient intermediate phases.
Real-time XRD patterns will reveal evolving oxidation kinetics.
The phase evolution observed by in-situ XRD will correlate with oxidation weight gain.
Traditional ex-situ methods cannot observe the proposed transient intermediate phases.
TGA combined with post-mortem XRD provides overall oxidation metrics but misses transient phenomena.
The method requires the sample to be reliably maintained under high-temperature oxidative conditions.
Phase changes faster than the temporal resolution of the setup may not be detected.
The rate and detectability of transient phase formation vary with material composition and temperature.
